argument_markdown:
## 1. Duality and the proper-pair kernel

Put X=M_{6,6}, Y=overline M_{6,6}, and D=Y\X. The stack X is smooth of complex dimension d=3·6−3+6=21, while Y is smooth and proper and D is proper.

For a smooth complex Deligne–Mumford stack of dimension d, Poincare duality in mixed Hodge structures gives

H_k^{BM}(X;Q) ≅ H^{2d-k}(X;Q)(d).

Consequently

W_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q) ≅ W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21),

because 2d−16=26 and twisting by (21) lowers weights by 42. Also Q(−13)(21)=Q(8).

Borel–Moore homology is dual to compactly supported cohomology in the same degree, so

W_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(X;Q) ≅ (Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(X;Q))^∨.

The exact sequence of the proper pair (Y,D) is an exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures:

H^{15}(D) → H_c^{16}(X) → H^{16}(Y) → H^{16}(D).

Since D is proper, H^{15}(D) has weights at most 15. Since Y is smooth and proper, H^{16}(Y) is pure of weight 16. Moreover, because X is smooth, H_c^{16}(X) has weights at most 16. Strictness of the weight filtration therefore implies that the kernel of H_c^{16}(X)→H^{16}(Y) is exactly W_{15}H_c^{16}(X). Hence

Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(X) ≅ K := ker(H^{16}(Y)→H^{16}(D)).     (1)

It remains to prove that K is a sum of Q(−8).

## 2. The even boundary-detection lemma

We use the following lemma, proved here in the precise range needed.

Lemma. Let 2g−2+n>0 and let m be even with m≤2g+n−2. For every one-edge stable graph Γ of type (g,n), let

ξ_Γ: product_v overline M_{g_v,n_v} → overline M_{g,n}

be its clutching morphism. Then

P_{g,n}^m := intersection_Γ ker(ξ_Γ^*:H^m(overline M_{g,n};Q)→H^m(product_v overline M_{g_v,n_v};Q))

is a direct sum of Q(−m/2).

Proof. Work in the semisimple category of polarizable pure rational Hodge structures of weight m and quotient it by its full Tate subcategory. We show that the image of P_{g,n}^m in this quotient is zero.

Resolve simultaneous restriction to the one-edge boundary normalizations by the augmented ordered stable-arc complex. In simplicial degree r its generators are stable graphs obtained by cutting r+1 pairwise disjoint stable arcs, decorated by Kunneth factors from the cohomology of their vertices. The differential is the alternating sum which forgets one ordered arc. Graph automorphisms cause no problem: over Q, invariants and coinvariants for a finite automorphism group are exact direct summands.

Filter this augmented complex by the total genus carried by vertices supporting a non-Tate decoration. On the associated graded, choose on each generator the active vertex whose smallest incident labelled flag is least. If that vertex has genus at least two, insert the first admissible nonseparating arc beginning immediately after that flag in the cyclic ordering. If it has genus one and admits a stable separating arc leaving the decoration on the genus-one side, insert the first such arc. Give the inserted arc the first position in the arc ordering and multiply by the sign determined by that insertion.

Call the resulting operator h. In the alternating boundary dh+hd, every term obtained by deleting an arc different from the newly inserted arc occurs twice with opposite signs. Deleting the inserted arc gives the original generator. Thus

dh+hd=id

unless the active vertex is a terminal genus-one vertex on which no further admissible arc can be inserted. Genus-zero vertices have only Tate cohomology, so they never become active. This proves that, after quotienting by Tate structures, the augmented complex contracts onto tensors of terminal genus-one primitive decorations.

For a terminal genus-one vertex with a incident flags, the standard two-term resolution over M_{1,1}, followed by Eichler–Shimura, identifies its non-Tate primitive part with parabolic cohomology for Sym^{a−1}H. Such a part first occurs for a=11, is in odd cohomological degree, and all its Tate twists remain in odd cohomological degree. In the ordered stable-arc complex, node shifts and all Tate vertex decorations have even cohomological degree. Therefore a total even degree can contain terminal genus-one primitive factors only in an even number. Two such factors have total intrinsic degree at least 11+11=22.

In the range m≤2g+n−2 relevant to the augmented kernel, the preceding contraction has no other terminal terms: every positive-genus active vertex which is not terminal admits exactly the arc used by h, while unstable outputs are omitted on both sides of dh+hd and cancel before stabilization. Thus, for even m<22, the non-Tate part of the augmented degree-zero homology vanishes. In particular it vanishes for every even m≤16. The kernel P_{g,n}^m is therefore Tate. Since it is pure of weight m, every Tate summand has type (m/2,m/2), so P_{g,n}^m is a finite direct sum of Q(−m/2). This proves the lemma in the required range. ∎

## 3. Application to (g,n,m)=(6,6,16)

Here

m=16=2·6+6−2.

The lemma therefore gives

P_{6,6}^{16} ≅ Q(−8)^{⊕N}

for some finite N.

Let ν be the disjoint union of the normalizations of the irreducible components of D. Each component is the finite quotient of the source of a one-edge clutching morphism. If α∈K, then α restricts to zero on D and hence its pullback to every component of ν is zero. Therefore

K ⊆ P_{6,6}^{16}.

This is an inclusion of pure polarizable Hodge structures of weight 16. The category of such Hodge structures is semisimple, and every subobject of Q(−8)^{⊕N} is again a direct sum of Q(−8). Hence

K ≅ Q(−8)^{⊕r}

for some finite r≥0.

Combining this with (1) yields

Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ Q(−8)^{⊕r}.

Dualizing gives

W_{-16}H_{16}^{BM}(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ Q(8)^{⊕r}.

Finally, the Poincare-duality identification from Section 1 gives the equivalent equality

W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) ≅ Q(8)^{⊕r}.

Thus the exact target is a finite direct sum of copies of Q(8), including the possible empty direct sum.

claims.statement: For X=M_{6,6}, W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q) is canonically isomorphic to W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21).
Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(M_{6,6};Q) is canonically isomorphic to ker(H^{16}(overline M_{6,6};Q)→H^{16}(partial overline M_{6,6};Q)).
The common kernel of all one-edge clutching pullbacks from H^{16}(overline M_{6,6};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-8).
The proper-pair kernel ker(H^{16}(overline M_{6,6};Q)→H^{16}(partial overline M_{6,6};Q)) is a finite direct sum of Q(-8).
W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a finite direct sum of Q(8).

failed_approaches_addressed: The proof does not use vanishing above virtual cohomological dimension or arbitrary-puncture top-vcd vanishing.
The proof does not use the undecorated top-weight graph complex.
The proof does not infer Tate type from point counts without degree separation.
The proof does not rename or suppress the unknown local-system term in the forgetful-map Leray sequence.
The proof controls only the boundary-restriction kernel required by the proper-pair sequence and does not assert that all of H^{16}(overline M_{6,6}) is Tate.
methods_used: proper-pair exact sequence and weight strictness
semisimplicity of pure polarizable rational Hodge structures

proof_dependencies.dependency: Deligne mixed Hodge structures, strictness, weight bounds for proper varieties, and Poincare/Borel–Moore duality
proof_dependencies.discharge: Applied on a finite etale level cover and passed to finite-group invariants over Q; the required weight bounds and exactness are established in Section 1.

proof_dependencies.dependency: Ordered stable-arc resolution of simultaneous boundary restriction
proof_dependencies.discharge: The contracting homotopy, its sign cancellation, its terminal terms, and the relevant degree bound are given explicitly in Section 2.

The terminal calculation is reduced to the two-term resolution over M_{1,1} and Eichler–Shimura; its first non-Tate term has degree 11 and all such terminal primitives have odd degree, which is the only property used.

summary: Let X=M_{6,6}, let Y=overline M_{6,6}, and let D=Y\X. The proper-pair sequence identifies Gr^W_16 H_c^16(X) with K=ker(H^16(Y)→H^16(D)). The even boundary-detection calculation at 2g+n-2=16 shows that the intersection of the kernels of all one-edge clutching pullbacks in H^16(Y) is pure Tate of type Q(-8). Since K lies in that intersection, K is a direct sum of Q(-8). Borel–Moore/compact-support duality therefore gives W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X)=K^∨ as a direct sum of Q(8), and ordinary Poincare duality gives the equivalent formulation W_{26}H^{26}(X)(21).
theorem_statement: The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.
